title: Dagger pipeline module: lint, test and build blocks
goal: Move CI logic into versioned, locally runnable pipeline blocks so every product shares one pipeline.
acceptance: `pipelines/dagger/` is a Dagger module in TypeScript exposing `lint`, `test` and `build` functions that take a source directory
`dagger call ci --src=.` runs lint, test and build for affected projects and exits non-zero on any failure
The GitHub Actions workflow calls `dagger call ci` instead of running Nx directly (PR labelled needs-human because it edits .github/)
A unit test for the module runs against a fixture workspace
scope: pipelines/dagger and the CI workflow call site.

title: SBOM and signing blocks for material packages
goal: Every released material package gets an SBOM and a signature consumers can verify.
acceptance: Dagger functions `sbom` (Syft, SPDX JSON) and `sign` (Cosign, key from an env var, keyless optional later) exist
`pnpm factory release orders-api` now writes `<package>.sbom.spdx.json` and `<package>.sig` next to each published tarball and uploads them to the registry storage
`pnpm factory verify @factory/orders-api-angular@<version>` checks the signature and fails on a tampered tarball (test proves it)
Test keys live only in test fixtures; real keys come from secrets and are never committed
scope: pipelines/dagger, tools/ release and verify commands.

title: Provenance statements for every release
goal: Record exactly which inputs produced each package, so impact analysis and recalls are possible.
acceptance: Each release writes an in-toto Statement (SLSA provenance predicate) listing: source commit, material name and version, every emitter id and version, and output digests
The statement is signed with the same key as the package
`pnpm factory provenance @factory/orders-api-angular@<version>` prints the statement in readable form
JSON Schema test validates the statement shape

title: Material graph service v1 (built with the nestjs-service recipe)
goal: A queryable graph of materials, packages, products and versions, built by the factory itself.
acceptance: `products/graph-service` is assembled from a product.yaml with the nestjs-service recipe
PostgreSQL schema (migrations checked in) stores nodes Material, MaterialVersion, Package, Product, ProductBuild and edges depends_on, emitted_by, consumed_by
`POST /ingest/provenance` accepts a provenance statement; `POST /ingest/lockfile` accepts a product's resolved material versions
`GET /materials/{name}/versions/{version}/consumers` returns every product build using it
Integration tests run against PostgreSQL via Testcontainers (or a docker compose service in CI)
scope: products/graph-service, materials for its API, docker compose.

title: Two more products consuming orders-api
goal: Gate 2 needs three consumers to prove propagation.
acceptance: `products/orders-admin-ui` (angular-remote) and `products/orders-report-worker` (nestjs-service) are assembled from product.yaml files consuming orders-api@^1
Both pass lint, test and build and have a contract test against orders-service
Their lockfiles are ingested into the graph service by `pnpm factory graph sync`
scope: products/ and tools/ graph sync command.

title: Impact analysis command and PR comment
goal: Show what a material change breaks before it merges.
acceptance: `pnpm factory impact materials/orders-api` classifies the change (patch, minor, breaking via oasdiff), lists affected products from the graph, and runs a dry-run assembly plus contract tests for each
Output is Markdown suitable for a PR comment and JSON for machines
A CI job posts the Markdown as a PR comment on material changes (needs-human: edits .github/)
Tests cover a patch change with zero failures and a breaking change that lists all three consumers
scope: tools/ impact command and one CI job.

title: Renovate propagation of material releases
goal: When a material releases, every consumer gets an upgrade PR automatically.
acceptance: `renovate.json` groups `@factory/*` packages, points at the Verdaccio registry, and auto-merges patch updates when CI is green
A documented dry run (`renovate --dry-run=full` against a fixture) shows upgrade branches for all three consumer products
docs/architecture.md explains how releases propagate

title: Lifecycle states and recall command
goal: Mark a bad material version recalled and drive every consumer off it.
acceptance: Material versions carry a state (draft, released, deprecated, recalled) stored in the graph service
`pnpm factory recall @factory/orders-api-angular@<version> --reason "..."` sets the state, runs `npm deprecate` on Verdaccio, and opens one GitHub issue per affected product labelled `recall`
`factory assemble` refuses to resolve a recalled version and prints the reason
Tests cover recall, refusal and the issue payloads (GitHub API mocked)

title: Container images and Helm library chart
goal: Every product kind ships the same way.
acceptance: Dagger function `image` builds an OCI image per product (static nginx-unprivileged for Angular remotes, distroless Node for NestJS services) and signs it
`deploy/charts/factory-lib` is a Helm library chart with templates for service and static-site workloads (probes, resources, security context)
Each product kind has a thin chart depending on factory-lib; `helm lint` and `kubeconform` pass in CI
Recipes generate the thin chart for new products

title: GitOps on a local kind cluster with signature enforcement
goal: Prove deploys are automatic and unsigned images are refused.
acceptance: `scripts/platform-up.sh` creates a kind cluster with Argo CD, Kyverno and a local registry
An ApplicationSet discovers every `products/*/deploy` folder and syncs it
A Kyverno policy rejects images without a valid Cosign signature; a test deploys an unsigned image and expects rejection
A CI job runs this end to end on kind (needs-human: edits .github/ and infrastructure)

title: Vulnerability scan block that can trigger a recall
goal: Close the loop from a found CVE to a recall.
acceptance: Dagger function `scan` runs Trivy on images and SBOMs and outputs findings as JSON
A nightly job scans every released package and image; a critical finding calls `factory recall` with the CVE id as the reason (dry-run flag for tests)
Test with a fixture SBOM containing a known critical CVE produces a recall in dry-run mode

title: Gate 2 demo: a spec change reaches three products with no manual steps
goal: Prove Gate 2 end to end.
acceptance: `scripts/gate2-demo.sh` adds a non-breaking field to orders.tsp, merges it, releases, and waits until all three consumers have merged upgrade PRs with green CI
The graph service shows all three products on the new version
A second run with a breaking change is stopped by the impact check before release
PROGRESS.md records the evidence and the planner opens `Gate 2 review` for a human

title: Fix vulnerability-scan review findings from PR #72
goal: Fix the four blocking problems from the PR #72 review; P2-11 merged before they were addressed.
acceptance: parseTrivy treats a report without Results as no findings
scan all skips versions already recalled
one package failure does not stop the run; missing store fails loudly
images scanned; recall order registry first, then graph state
nightly-scan.yml declares permissions and registry auth
`pnpm nx affected -t lint test build --base=origin/main` exits 0

title: Assembly security: fail-closed integrity and safe tarball extraction
goal: Fix the two blocking security findings from the PR #60 review (P1-09), which merged unfixed.
acceptance: `factory assemble` refuses a package version whose registry metadata has no usable integrity: verify `sha512-` integrity, else `dist.shasum` (sha1), else throw; test proves a version with no integrity is rejected

Before extraction the tarball is listed and rejected if it contains symlinks, hardlinks, absolute paths or `..` segments; extraction uses `--no-same-owner`; test with a crafted malicious tarball proves rejection
The tarball URL must have the same origin as the configured registry; test proves a foreign origin is rejected
`pnpm nx affected -t lint test build --base=origin/main` exits 0

title: Sign exactly the bytes that are published; no unsigned release possible
goal: Fix blocking finding 1 from the PR #63 review (P2-02), which merged unfixed.
acceptance: `factory release` validates the signing key before anything is packed or published; a bad key fails with nothing published (test)

Each package is packed once into the attestation store; the SBOM, signature and provenance are made from that tarball; that exact file is published with `npm publish <tarball>` (test asserts signed bytes equal published bytes)
If attestation fails, nothing is published; a re-run of a version that is published but unsigned is detected and reported instead of silently skipped (test)
`scripts/gate1-demo.sh` still passes
`pnpm nx affected -t lint test build --base=origin/main` exits 0
scope: tools/factory/src/release.ts, attest.ts, provenance.ts and their tests.

title: Decide where attestations live (ADR for a human)
goal: Resolve finding 2 from the PR #63 review: the issue asked for .sig and SBOM in the registry storage, but they are written to a filesystem store that CI and other machines cannot reach.
acceptance: `docs/adr/0001-attestation-storage.md` compares at least: filesystem store (today), companion npm package per release, OCI artifacts in Harbor/zot via `oras`, and a small sidecar service; for each: how `factory verify`, the nightly scan and the graph find attestations, effort, and offline/air-gapped fit
It recommends one option and lists the follow-up tasks it implies
No code changes in this task; the PR is labelled needs-human so a human records the decision

title: Retro-review the Phase 2 PRs that merged without review
goal: PRs #62 (P2-01 Dagger), #66 (P2-09 images and Helm), #67 (P2-10 kind GitOps) and #69 (P2-06 impact) merged with no reviewer run. Review them now and file what is wrong.
acceptance: Each of the four merged diffs is reviewed against its issue's acceptance criteria, CLAUDE.md, contracts, tests and security, using the `reviewer` subagent
Every blocking problem found becomes its own issue `[P2-nn]` (next free ID) labelled `ready` and `phase-2`, with testable acceptance criteria, and is added to the Blocked by list of `[P2-12]`
A summary comment is posted on each of the four PRs (no findings is a valid outcome)
No code changes in this task

title: Make the Dagger pipeline module actually run
goal: P2-01 was never run against a Dagger engine; its first real run in the `dagger` CI job (PR #73) failed.
acceptance: Read the failing `dagger` job log from the latest CI run on main (or reproduce with `dagger call -m pipelines/dagger ci --src=. --base=origin/main` where Docker exists) and fix `pipelines/dagger/src` until the job passes
`lint`, `test` and `build` functions each run end to end in the engine; the module's unit tests still pass
PR notes say whether the `verify` job can now switch to `dagger call ci` (the switch itself is a needs-human workflow change)
`pnpm nx affected -t lint test build --base=origin/main` exits 0

title: graph-service runs from its built output and as a container
goal: Fix the follow-up from P2-05: the built graph-service cannot find `migrations/` (`../../migrations` from dist), so it only runs from the source layout.
acceptance: Migrations are copied into the build output (Nx assets) or embedded, and resolved relative to the built file; `node dist/products/graph-service/main.js` applies migrations against a test database (test)
The Dagger `image` function builds a graph-service image that starts and answers its health endpoint (or, without Docker, a test that runs the built output from a temp directory outside the repo)
`pnpm nx affected -t lint test build --base=origin/main` exits 0
scope: products/graph-service (src/ext and project config), pipelines/dagger if needed.

title: Graph-service API as a TypeSpec material
goal: Follow-up from P2-04: the graph API is hand-written in `src/ext/`. The factory should build its own services from materials.
acceptance: `materials/graph-api/` defines the existing endpoints (ingest provenance, ingest lockfile, consumers, version state) in TypeSpec with a valid material.yaml; Spectral and oasdiff pass
graph-service implements the generated nest-server controllers; hand-written logic stays in `src/ext/`
`tools/factory` calls graph-service through the generated client instead of ad-hoc fetch calls where practical
Existing graph and recall tests pass unchanged in behaviour
`pnpm nx affected -t lint test build --base=origin/main` exits 0

title: Charts for every product and a passing kind end-to-end run
goal: Follow-up from P2-09/P2-10: only two products have a committed `chart/`, the ApplicationSet path differs from the issue wording, and the kind scripts were never run on a cluster.
acceptance: Every product under `products/` has a `chart/` generated by its recipe (orders-ui, orders-service and graph-service included); `scripts/chart-check.sh` passes in the `charts` CI job
The ApplicationSet path and the architecture doc agree (document `products/*/chart`)
The manual `platform-e2e` workflow passes: platform up, unsigned image rejected; fix scripts until it does (a human triggers the workflow run and links the result in the PR)
`pnpm nx affected -t lint test build --base=origin/main` exits 0
scope: products/*/chart, recipes/ chart output, deploy/platform, scripts/platform-*.sh, docs.

title: Propagation without manual steps: factory propagate
goal: Gate 2 needs a spec change to reach consumers with no manual steps, but Renovate needs a real platform and re-assembly after a lockfile bump is not automated (P2-07 follow-up).
acceptance: `factory propagate <material>@<version>` finds consumers (graph, else lockfiles), and for each: bumps the pin, re-runs `factory assemble`, runs the product's tests, and opens a PR via the GitHub REST API labelled `needs-review` (dry-run flag for tests)
Patch bumps whose tests pass are labelled `claude-approved` so auto-merge applies; minor and major bumps are not
Running it twice opens no duplicate PRs (test)
Renovate config stays for real deployments; docs/architecture.md explains when each is used
`pnpm nx affected -t lint test build --base=origin/main` exits 0

title: Impact report runs the dry-run assembly in CI
goal: Follow-up from P2-06: in CI no registry is reachable, so the impact report skips the dry-run assembly and only checks ranges and contract tests.
acceptance: `tools/factory/ci/impact.yml` starts Verdaccio as a service container, releases the changed material's current and proposed versions into it, and runs the impact report with the dry-run assembly enabled
A fixture PR scenario (test) shows the dry-run section reported as run, not skipped
The workflow change is provided in `tools/factory/ci/` for a human to copy (needs-human)

title: Live HTTP contract tests for consumer products
goal: Follow-up from P2-05: consumer contract tests compare lockfile pins instead of calling orders-service over HTTP.
acceptance: orders-ui, orders-admin-ui and orders-report-worker each have a contract test that starts orders-service (or its generated Nest base with fixtures) and calls it through the emitted client over real HTTP
A breaking change in orders-api makes at least one consumer contract test fail (test with a fixture spec)
The tests run in CI under `nx affected`
`pnpm nx affected -t lint test build --base=origin/main` exits 0

title: Recall is idempotent
goal: Non-blocking finding from the PR #71 review: re-running `factory recall` opens duplicate issues.
acceptance: Before opening a recall issue for a product, `factory recall` searches open issues labelled `recall` for the same package and version and skips existing ones (test)
Re-running a recall on an already-recalled version changes nothing and exits 0 with a clear message (test)
`pnpm nx affected -t lint test build --base=origin/main` exits 0

title: CI hardening: pinned checksums and safe expressions
goal: Non-blocking findings from the PR #73 review.
acceptance: kubeconform and Dagger downloads in `ci.yml` are verified against pinned SHA-256 checksums; Dagger is installed from a pinned release archive, not `curl | sh`
`impact.yml` passes `github.base_ref` through `env:` instead of interpolating it into the script
Changes are proposed in `tools/factory/ci/` (or as a PR touching `.github/workflows/` labelled needs-human) for a human to apply

title: Builder claims an issue before working on it
goal: Two builder runs once implemented the same issue (PRs #50 and #51). Make the claim atomic and visible.
acceptance: `prompts/builder.md`: before creating a branch, the builder adds `in-progress` and a comment `claimed by run <timestamp>`; it then re-reads the issue and backs off if another claim comment is older than its own
Claims with no commits for 3 hours are treated as stale and may be taken over (documented)
PR labelled needs-human (it changes how the loops behave)
